description: Six-panel composite of EBSD band-contrast (BC) maps with austenite highlighted in red; every panel carries a 50 µm scale bar and a sample label printed in the top-right corner: (a) HR, (b) IQ-1050, (c) QA-620, (d) QA-680, (e) QA-740, (f) QA-800. All panels show the same micro-laminated banded structure: elongated light-grey bands interpreted (high BC) as δ-ferrite, separated by a darker, fine lath-like matrix interpreted (low BC) as lath/tempered martensite. In (a) HR the red austenite is concentrated in patchy bands inside the martensitic regions; (b) IQ-1050 shows the coarsest ferrite bands and only sparse, isolated red austenite. In the QA series (c)-(f) the red austenite becomes progressively more abundant and more widely dispersed in the tempered martensite as the annealing temperature rises from 620 to 800 °C, appearing fine and scattered in QA-620 but blocky and coarse in QA-680, QA-740 and QA-800. The figure prints no axes, legend, colour bar or numeric values; it demonstrates qualitatively how treatment changes δ-ferrite band morphology and the spatial distribution of austenite, complementing the EBSD/XRD austenite volume fractions given in Table 2.

subfigures.description: BC map of specimen HR with red austenite overlay, 50 µm scale bar. Horizontal light-grey δ-ferrite bands are segmented by dark lath martensite; red austenite forms patchy, concentrated bands within the darker matrix rather than inside the light ferrite bands.

BC map of specimen IQ-1050, 50 µm scale bar. Coarser, thicker light δ-ferrite bands with dark martensite between them; red austenite is the scarcest of all panels, present only as small isolated patches.
BC map of specimen QA-620, 50 µm scale bar. Banded δ-ferrite plus tempered martensite; red austenite is fine and widely scattered through the martensitic regions.
BC map of specimen QA-680, 50 µm scale bar. Red austenite areas are larger and more numerous than in QA-620, distributed through the tempered martensite and appearing as blocky regions.
BC map of specimen QA-740, 50 µm scale bar. Extensive widely distributed red austenite within the tempered martensite matrix, with elongated ferrite bands still clearly visible.
BC map of specimen QA-800, 50 µm scale bar. Large, coarse red austenite blocks and bands, especially in the upper part of the field; the highest visible red area fraction among the panels.

observations.observation: The figure is a six-panel composite of grey-scale band-contrast (BC) maps, each with a 50 µm scale bar, labelled in the top-right corner as HR (a), IQ-1050 (b), QA-620 (c), QA-680 (d), QA-740 (e) and QA-800 (f).
Every panel shows the same micro-laminated banded structure: elongated light-grey bands separated by a darker, finer lath-like matrix.
The caption states that the red overlay is the austenite distribution and that the underlying images are BC maps of the experimental steels under various treatments.
The citing text states that bright/white regions of high BC value are considered ferrite while dark regions of low BC value are considered lath martensite.
In panel (a) HR the red austenite is concentrated in patchy bands within the dark martensitic regions rather than inside the light δ-ferrite bands.
Panel (b) IQ-1050 contains markedly less red austenite than any other panel, the red appearing only as small isolated patches.
The citing text states that δ-ferrite and prior austenite grains grew up after heating at 1050 °C and that ferrite bands were segmented by martensite lamellar, becoming dispersed.
From (c) QA-620 to (f) QA-800 the red austenite area visibly increases and becomes more widely distributed within the tempered martensite.
Panels (d) QA-680, (e) QA-740 and (f) QA-800 show coarse, blocky red austenite regions, whereas (c) QA-620 shows finer, more scattered red regions.
The citing text states that the austenite distribution in HR was more concentrated than in the QA specimens, and that there was little austenite in IQ-1050.

The caption states that austenitic volume fractions of QA specimens were measured by EBSD and XRD and are listed in Table 2; the present figure itself prints no numeric data other than panel labels and 50 µm scale bars.
No axes, legend, colour scale or quantitative data labels are present on any panel of this figure; the readout is limited to the red/grey colour coding plus scale bars.
